description: The DIB Scuto1 deposit holds research data for design optimization, indoor characterization and outdoor testing of a four-terminal photovoltaic device. The CNR Institute for Microelectronics and Microsystems team in Catania combines gallium-arsenide and bifacial silicon heterojunction technologies with optical spectrum splitting. The article relates the measurements to changing solar spectra and bifacial energy gains. Mendeley explicitly links the named article and provides a ZIP container free under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is a device experiment in Catania, not a long-term commercial solar-farm series. The repository does not document internal file formats, a common sampling interval or exact observation dates, and those details remain unverified. A reviewer-assessed use is checking component-performance assumptions for four-terminal or bifacial photovoltaic simulations. model-system-advisor-model-sam is a related photovoltaic modelling resource, although direct representation of this experimental architecture was not checked. No archive or article PDF was downloaded.
